---
title: "Earth2Studio.jl"
---

## Overview

**Earth2Studio.jl** is a thin Julia wrapper around [NVIDIA's earth2studio](https://github.com/NVIDIA/earth2studio) Python package for AI-powered weather and climate forecasting. It uses [PythonCall.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/PythonCall.jl) to expose the full `earth2studio` Python API — data sources, prognostic and diagnostic models, perturbations, IO backends, run workflows, and verification statistics — as Python objects you can call from Julia.

The package itself is intentionally minimal: it imports `earth2studio` and its top-level submodules and holds them as `Py` references. Nothing is exported, because upstream names such as `run` and `io` would clash with `Base`. All functionality lives in the upstream Python package.

## Quickstart

On first `using Earth2Studio`, [CondaPkg.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/CondaPkg.jl) creates a Conda environment with Python (3.11–3.13), `earth2studio[data]` (version 0.18 or newer), and the conda-forge packages the data sources need. No manual pip step is required. Model extras are opt-in — add a `CondaPkg.toml` to your own project and CondaPkg merges it with the one shipped here:

```toml
[pip.deps.earth2studio]
extras = ["fcn", "pangu"]
```

Every reference is accessed through the module, e.g. `Earth2Studio.data`. `DateTime` and `String` convert to the Python types earth2studio expects. See the [Basics](tutorials/basics.qmd) tutorial for the full set of interop patterns, including when a Julia vector must be converted with `pylist`, and the [Forecasting](tutorials/forecasting.qmd) tutorial for running a model.

Fetch a field from ARCO ERA5, bring it back to Julia with [PythonCall.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/PythonCall.jl), and plot it with [CairoMakie](https://docs.makie.org):

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
# On first zarr chunk decode, numcodecs creates a multiprocessing.Lock, which spawns a
# resource_tracker subprocess. That child inherits the stdout/stderr pipe the notebook
# runner uses to capture cell output and keeps it open, so the render hangs waiting for
# EOF. Spawn the tracker here with stdio pointed at /dev/null so it never holds the pipe.
using PythonCall: pyimport
redirect_stdio(stdout=devnull, stderr=devnull) do
    pyimport("multiprocessing.resource_tracker").ensure_running()
end
```

```{julia}
using Earth2Studio
using Dates
using CairoMakie
using PythonCall: pyconvert

ds = Earth2Studio.data.ARCO(verbose=false)
da = ds(DateTime(2023, 6, 15), "t2m")   # xarray.DataArray with dims (time, variable, lat, lon)

lon = pyconvert(Vector, da.lon.values)
lat = pyconvert(Vector, da.lat.values)
t2m = pyconvert(Array, da.values)[1, 1, :, :] .- 273.15   # lat × lon, °C

fig = Figure(size=(900, 450))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; title="ERA5 2 m temperature, 2023-06-15 00:00 UTC", xlabel="Longitude", ylabel="Latitude")
hm = heatmap!(ax, lon, lat, permutedims(t2m))
Colorbar(fig[1, 2], hm; label="°C")
fig
```
